description: Red and gold Chinese temple with upswept ridge ends, round columns wrapped in relief dragons, and hanging incense coils across the open front hall.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Squat rectangular Chinese temple under a heavy tiled roof with strongly upswept curled ridge ends and a pair of facing figures on the ridge, an open front hall behind a row of thick round columns carved with dragons coiling up their full height, large conical incense coils hung in rows from the ceiling beams, a wide stone incense urn on the forecourt, raised threshold beam across the entrance Materials: Deep vermilion lacquered columns and beams with gold leaf detailing, green glazed roof tiles, ash-grey incense coils, soot blackening across the ceiling and upper columns, worn stone threshold polished by feet.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT v2. Overall visual fidelity 0.90: silhouette 0.92 on a 0.045 / 0.044 band table, structure 0.92, form 0.88, material 0.88, lighting 0.86. 8,012/16,000 triangles, 9/12 draw calls, 7/8 materials, 9/32 unique geometries, 5 canvases. check-coplanar clean.

featureReviews.evidence: Xieshan hip-and-gable from the proxy centre-column profile: eave lip 0.615 H, concave 18 -> 33 deg to an apex at 0.84 H, hip skirt at 21 deg to a vertical pediment base at 0.69 H, gable face at z +-4.09 against eaves at +-5.93, ridge bar 0.84-0.89 H. Band table 0.045 / 0.044.
featureReviews.notes: v1 was a concave HIP on all four sides with its apex at 0.885 H, scored 0.87 against a review that had never looked at the proxy elevations. The end depth map reads a vertical face at 0.445 H from 0.69 H up -- a pediment -- and band 8 puts all surface within +-0.05 H of the ridge line, which is a tall ridge bar over a LOWER apex than the end-view extremes suggested (those extremes were the flat swallow-tail ends seen end-on). Bands 0-8 now sit within 0.09 H of the proxy on both axes; the residual is band 9, where the horn tips reach 0.77 H along the ridge against the proxy's 0.94. Not higher than 0.92 because the upper slope above the pediment is straight where the plate still shows a slight sag, and the hip skirt is a single power curve rather than a measured table.

featureReviews.evidence: Eaves line lifts 0.70 m over the outer 60 % of each half-side into four corner curls (tips 0.73 H, proxy 0.72-0.75); two swallow-tail ridge horns sweeping 35 -> 135 deg to 1.0 H with a second prong; two pediment-foot horns; verge boards on both rakes.
featureReviews.notes: The preamble's curledHorn samples a sine and built spikes; spiralHorn() turns the heading past vertical so the ridge ends curl back over as the plate's do. The eaves sweep is eight points per side on a 2.5-power ramp, indexed so the corner warp shades smooth -- the loose-triangle first build faceted every quad at the corners. Held at 0.88: the tails are swept box segments, not the flat fan the plate shows, and the corner curls are short.

featureReviews.evidence: Two helical dragon tubes (2.4 turns, tapering, twenty fins, blocked head) on the centre front columns; ten 0.84 x 0.75 m grooved coils at two heights; eight columns on drums in two rows; side walls to the front; door wall with a closed pair and two open doorways; sooted bracket beam with five gilt panels; censer 1.9 m.
featureReviews.notes: v1 stood a red box BEHIND five columns; the proxy front plane reads the wall ends at +-0.545 H, i.e. the colonnade sits inside the walls with a mid-depth door wall, and that is what is built. The coils first rendered BLACK -- a 128 x 512 canvas painted only over its top 128 px -- and now carry a square groove tile plus a small emissive standing in for the open sky the harness cannot supply. Not higher than 0.90 because the dragon head is a block and the brackets are two stacked boxes.

featureReviews.evidence: Tile courses at 0.25 m pitch over the whole roof via metre UVs along the eaves by slope distance; round cap tiles on the clamped fascia band; soot gradient 1.0 -> 0.62 up the walls plus streak canvas; stone mottle, stain and grime; coil grooves. 5 canvases, 72 ms.
featureReviews.notes: v1 listed the pantile course as its largest omission and shipped a smooth sweep. The courses are a multiplier canvas so every material keeps its measured albedo; the first soot tile used round clouds and read as leopard spots, replaced by vertical washes only. Held at 0.88: the courses are stripes, not scalloped tile ends, and the caps are painted, not modelled.

featureReviews.evidence: Seven materials at PBR confidence 0.751-0.860, every albedo shipped at or between its measured swatches -- red #5E221C (measured #4B1B17 / #6A2621), dark #452520 (#250D0A / #391412), coil #746A62, green #4F6B56 (#506D57).
featureReviews.notes: v1 lifted three albedos to grey against a luma-only reading of the silhouette gate; the gate's segmenter is RGB distance >24 from #3a3a3a OR saturation >0.16, so a dark saturated red is never a hole, and the measured values ship. holeviz on all four frames shows enclosed background only between the beasts' legs (472 px at 090). The green renders paler than the plate's jade under the harness's flat lighting, which is the point held back.

name: Chinese Shrine
notes: A Chinese-Thai neighbourhood shrine hall, and it must not be built with the profile of a Thai wat: the roof here is heavy and low with strongly upswept curled ridge ends, where a Thai temple roof is steep, tiered and finished with straight horn finials. The dragon-wrapped round columns and the hanging incense coils across the open front are the two features that carry recognition from outside. Declared at 12 m long, above the building-part category 8 m prior, which is correct for a neighbourhood shrine hall. Width and height re-declared 2026-08-28 from the Meshy proxy bbox (1.90 x 1.45 x 1.38 units = long : h : short = 1 : 0.764 : 0.726) at the kept 12 m length: h = 12 x 0.764 = 9.2 m (was 8), across = 12 x 0.726 = 8.7 m (was 10). The old 10 x 8 read wider and squatter than the plate in every band table row. The roof is a xieshan hip-and-gable, not a plain hip. No destruction groups: it is static landmark geometry.
